issues.detail: The Vietnamese translation places 'vui lòng' (pleased/willed) at the end of the sentence as a trailing modifier, but in the Greek text, 'δε ευδοκησεν' (did not please/will) is the main verb governing the entire clause. The Vietnamese structure makes it sound like God was pleased *by* the actions of separating and calling, whereas the Greek indicates that God *did not* will/please [the action]. Furthermore, the negation 'δε' (not) is missing or obscured in the Vietnamese translation.
